report.clinical_summary: The patient presents with persistent tiredness for a few weeks that has been gradually worsening, described as lethargy that persists even after resting. They also have a pea-sized lump on one side of their neck that has been present longer than they realized (wife just noticed it). Additional symptoms include eating more than usual, feeling warmer than usual, and difficulty sleeping. They have a family history of CLL (father died from complications). They are not on any regular medications, only occasional OTC pain relief. They trust doctors and follow recommendations, believing doctors are appropriately cautious about prescribing.
